overall.summary: The rule-list reading holds up well (the stated rule agrees with the model on 99.5% of training rows and its thresholds are the best-fitting ones), but one root statement is wrong: switching off the bmi, under-age and few-visits hinges together gives AUC 0.623, not 0.500; the cited query switched off all seven leaves. A few smaller statements are imprecise.

findings.statement: Switching off the bmi, under-age and few-visits hinges together lowers the training AUC to 0.500.
findings.check: verify ablate with the three named leaves; compared with the cited query q_a5bd54a192 (evidence[18])
findings.evidence: With the three leaves off the AUC is 0.6229 (accuracy 0.578, 9816 flips). The cited query switched off all seven leaves (switched_off[0..6]), which makes every first-layer exit 0 and the prediction constant, hence AUC 0.5 trivially. Wrong population for the sentence (scope mismatch); the provenance-rendered number is faithful to a query that does not match the text.

findings.statement: Units 7 and 9 are large for young women and larger still for young non-smoking women
findings.check: node values for the four smoker x sex cells at age 25 (typical otherwise); first-layer weights
findings.evidence: At age 25: unit 7 = 1.90 (male non-smoker), 4.05 (female non-smoker), 0 (male smoker), 1.53 (female smoker); unit 9 = 1.65, 3.44, 0, 0.53. Weights: unit 7 age -1.39, smoker -1.15, female +1.08; unit 9 smoker -1.33, age -1.17, female +0.89. They are young-non-smoker detectors boosted by being female; a young female smoker gets less than a young male non-smoker. The downstream reading (unit 23 fires for young female smokers) is unaffected.

findings.statement: over the sweep the predicted risk drifts from 11% at age 20 to 4% at age 70. So in the whole model these units give a small downward slope in risk with age outside the rules
findings.check: part contribution and risk without the part over an age sweep, typical case
findings.evidence: The part contributes 0 at ages 20-50 (units 1 and 8 are 0 there); without it the risk still falls 10.8% -> 8.0% from age 20 to 50. Its contribution is -0.19 at 60, -0.51 at 70, -0.37 at 80, -0.24 at 90 (logit): it lowers the risk only above about 55, most at 70 (4.4% vs 7.1% without), and the effect shrinks again after 70. Part of the stated 11% -> 4% drift comes from other units.

findings.statement: income, urban and noise move the typical case little but shift risk near the bmi step
findings.check: probe at bmi 32 (typical otherwise) over income, urban and noise
findings.evidence: Income does shift it (50.4% at income 10 to 15.0% at 150, urban off) and urban moves it 43.9% -> 47.7%, but noise from -2 to 2 gives 43.6%, 47.6%, 42.5%: a few points, no larger than in the typical case. The root hypothesis only gives evidence for income and urban at the step; noise is overstated in the summary.

high_bmi_hinges.why: Two bmi hinges that create the model's main rule, a step from about 10% to about 92% predicted risk at bmi 32 to 32.5, which holds across ages, sexes and incomes.

under_age_hinge.why: A single age hinge that is on below age 61 and blocks the older-and-frequent-visitor rule; the risk jumps at 60 to 61 only when visits are 3 or more.

few_visits_hinges.why: Visits hinges that are on for 0 to 2 visits and block the same rule; the jump at 2 to 3 visits appears at age 70 and not at age 45.

older_age_hinges.why: They lower the predicted risk of people over about 55 outside the rules (most at about 70), but the stated drift from age 20 is partly due to other units and their role inside the second layer is not read.

sex_smoking_age_detectors.why: Through second-layer unit 23 they create a young-female-smoker rule (unit 23 on for 347 of 350 such rows, risk about 94% fading to 9% by age 38), although the description of units 7 and 9 alone is imprecise.

score_insurance_hinges.why: Unit 6 is a confirmed veto (a high score without insurance pulls the bmi and age-visits rules to low risk), but the low-score unit 14 has no reading of its own.

mixed_hinges.why: For insured people the part sharpens the rule (adds about 0.6 logit on rule-high rows, takes 0.3 off the rest), but its three units have no separate reading.
